reflection_text.1:
The JTB analysis needs three independent dimensions B,T,J with K = B∧T∧J. If the ontology is closed to just Knowledge and Belief, then K → B and everything non-K is forced into a single residual B.

That makes Belief heterogeneous. The 2×2 truth × justification space collapses:
* JT = K
* J¬T = justified false belief
* ¬JT = unjustified true belief
* ¬J¬T = unjustified false belief

With only K/B, J¬T, ¬JT and ¬J¬T all have to be called “mere belief”. 

The consensus taxonomic loss is therefore twofold:
1. Justification is lost once truth fails. A justified false belief is epistemically creditworthy but false, so on JTB it is not K. On a K/B only taxonomy it is just B, indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief. There is no state for justified non-knowledge, so justification cannot be marked as an independent epistemic good.
2. Truth is lost once justification fails. An unjustified true belief is true but lucky/defective, so on JTB it is not K. On a K/B only taxonomy it is just B, indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief. There is no state for true non-knowledge, so truth cannot be marked as an independent epistemic good.

This coarse-graining is often re-described as a grounding problem for the Justification condition. If justification is to be cashable in the only resources K and B, it must be either
* justification as K: to be justified is to know you are justified, etc., which generates a regress/circularity and ultimately Meno’s paradox; or
* justification as B: to be justified is to believe you are justified / to believe the grounds, which makes justification collapse into belief, permits bootstrapping and makes K collapse into true belief + further belief.

Trying to stop the regress then forces an arbitrary foundational stop: a base of beliefs taken as justified simply by being held, i.e. dogmatic foundationalism, or a circular mutual support among beliefs. 

So the discussion has two clusters: the taxonomic collapse of J¬T and ¬JT into bare Belief, and the regress/circularity/dogmatism problem that follows from having no independent justified-belief state to halt justification. The former is the clear loss of discriminatory power; the latter is how colleagues formalise the loss as infinite regress vs arbitrary foundation. Unresolved is whether the “two problems” are meant as the two missing cells J¬T and ¬JT, or as regress and foundational dogmatism; both are presented as consequences of the same two-state restriction.
reflection_text.4:
The JTB analysis requires three independent dimensions B,T,J. With the ontology restricted to Knowledge = JTB and Belief as the sole non-knowledge residue, Belief is forced to be the disjunction ¬K = [J∧¬T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧¬T∧B]. K entails B, so the taxonomy is coarse-grained.

The coarse-graining is seen as two distinct losses of discriminatory power that colleagues repeatedly agree on:

* Justified false belief, J∧B∧¬T. Intuitively epistemically creditworthy error. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is false, so with only K/B it must be filed as mere Belief. Belief is therefore forced to contain justified states and justified false belief becomes indistinguishable from unjustified false belief ¬J∧¬T∧B. Justification is invisible once truth fails; there is no state ‘justified belief’ in which to house warranted error.

* Unjustified true belief, T∧B∧¬J. Intuitively lucky true belief. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is unjustified, so with only K/B it must also be filed as mere Belief. Belief is therefore forced to contain true states and an unjustified lucky true belief becomes indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief. Truth is invisible once justification fails; the epistemic defect of luck cannot be marked off from mere false belief.

Hence Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag of J~T, T~J and ~J~T, losing the independent normative roles of justification apart from truth and truth apart from justification. That is normally phrased as justification does not entail truth and truth does not entail justification.

Because justification has no independent epistemic state to be cashed out in, the justification condition is self-consuming on a K/B only inventory. If justification for p must be supplied by a further epistemic attitude, it must be a Knowledge or a Belief. Knowledge = JTB already presupposes justification, so making justification = knowledge is circular/regressive: p is justified because it is known, p is known only if it is justified. If justification is cashed out as belief, the demand that justifiers themselves be justified generates an infinite regress of justifying beliefs B1, B2… with no stopping point. To stop the regress the inventory forces an arbitrary foundational dogmatism: a class of beliefs taken as justified simply by being held, or known by stipulation, with no internal JTB support. So colleagues converge on a grounding pressure: endless higher-order justification vs circularity/bootstrapping vs an undefended foundational base.

The two cells J~T and T~J are the canonical examples of the loss, and the regress/dogmatism/circularity pressure is the structural consequence of trying to express justification using only Knowledge and Belief. Unresolved nuance is whether the intended ‘two problems’ are best stated as the two coarse-graining losses or as regress vs arbitrary foundation; current consensus in the round treats them as mutually entailing.
reflection_text.3:
The discussion converges on the coarse-graining that results when JTB is forced onto a Knowledge/Belief only ontology. K = B ∧ T ∧ J, so K→B and everything not K must be called B. The 2×2 Truth × Justification space therefore collapses:

* J∧T → Knowledge
* J∧¬T = justified false belief
* ¬J∧T = unjustified true belief
* ¬J∧¬T = unjustified false belief

All three latter cells are forced into the single residual label ‘Belief’. 

That gives the loss of independent tracking of justification and truth:

1. Justification is invisible when truth fails. A justified false belief is epistemically creditworthy but not knowledge, yet on a K/B taxonomy it is just B and indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief. Justification ceases to be recognisable as an epistemic good in the false case.

2. Truth is invisible when justification fails. An unjustified true belief is true but epistemically defective, yet on a K/B taxonomy it is also just B and indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief. The distinction between warranted truth and lucky truth is lost; belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag of J¬T, ¬J T and ¬J ¬T.

Several colleagues re-describe the same pressure as a grounding problem for the Justification condition. With only K and B available, justification for p must be supplied by a further belief q or by knowledge. If justification is cashed in beliefs, justification of p requires justification of q, etc., yielding an infinite regress of justifiers. If the chain is stopped, the stopping point must be an unjustified belief taken as basic, i.e. an arbitrary/dogmatic foundation, or a knowledge claim that already presupposes justification, i.e. circularity / bootstrapping. So the regress/terminus dilemma is the operational form of the inability to have an independent justified-belief state.

Disagreement in emphasis is mainly terminological: some frame the problems as the two collapses J¬T vs ¬J¬T and ¬J T vs J¬T, others frame them as regress vs foundational dogmatism/circularity. Both point to the same loss: no independent epistemic status for justified belief and for true belief, and Belief is forced to do the work of three distinct profiles. Unresolved for me is whether the question wants the two-cell collapse description or the regress/dogmatism description; the literature normally presents them together.
reflection_text.8:
The deliberation is converging on the coarse-graining that results when the JTB tripartite ingredients B,T,J must be expressed with only two primitive labels K and B, with K = B∧T∧J and K→B.

On that inventory the 2×2 truth × justification space collapses:

* J T = K
* J ¬T = justified false belief
* ¬J T = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ¬T = unjustified false belief

Everything not K is forced into the residual label ‘Belief’. Belief therefore has to do the work of three distinct profiles J¬T, ¬J T and ¬J¬T.

The consensus loss that is repeatedly identified is twofold and essentially the same point in two directions.

1. Justification is lost when truth fails. A justified false belief is epistemically creditworthy – properly supported though false – but on JTB it is not knowledge. With only K/B it must be called mere Belief. Hence justified false belief is indistinguishable from unjustified false belief; the justification condition becomes invisible once ¬T obtains. This is the ‘justified false belief / warranted error’ problem.

2. Truth is lost when justification fails. An unjustified true belief is true but epistemically defective – lucky, accidental – but on JTB it is not knowledge. With only K/B it must also be called mere Belief. Hence an unjustified true belief is indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief; truth becomes invisible once ¬J obtains. This is the ‘unjustified true belief / lucky truth’ problem.

The same difficulty is often reformulated as a grounding problem for the justification condition under a K/B only ontology. If justification for p must be supplied by a further epistemic state, the justifier can only be a belief or a piece of knowledge. That pushes either:

* an infinite regress of ever higher-order justifiers – justify p by belief q, justify q by r, … – with no third epistemic status to stop the chain; or
* a circular grounding where justification is made to coincide with knowledge, or a need to halt the chain at a dogmatic foundational belief that is taken as justified simply by being held.

Several colleagues describe this regress/terminus dilemma as the formal expression of the coarse-graining above: with no independent ‘justified belief’ status, justification cannot be tracked independently of truth, and belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag of justified/unjustified × true/false.

Unresolved tension: whether to state the two problems as the two lost cells J¬T and ¬J T, or as the classic regress vs arbitrary foundational stop. The discussion suggests they are two ways of describing the same structural loss: the inability to keep justification and truth as independently trackable epistemic values when the only non-knowledge label is Belief. No Gettier discussion is needed here.
reflection_text.10:
The question is about the coarse-graining that results when the only doxastic labels allowed are Knowledge and mere Belief while Knowledge is defined as JTB = B∧T∧J.

With K = JTB, K entails B, so non-K is the residual category Belief. The truth×justification 2×2 therefore collapses:

* JT = Knowledge
* J¬T = justified false belief
* ¬JT = unjustified true belief
* ¬J¬T = unjustified false belief

All three non-JT cells are forced into the single label ‘Belief’. Belief is therefore a heterogeneous catch-all.

The two discriminatory losses that are repeatedly highlighted are:

1. Loss of a distinct place for justified false belief. J¬TB is epistemically creditworthy but false, so on JTB it is not Knowledge. On a K/B only taxonomy it is just ‘Belief’, indistinguishable from ¬J¬TB unjustified false belief. Justification is invisible once truth fails; a well-supported error cannot be marked off from an arbitrary error.

2. Loss of a distinct place for unjustified true belief. ¬JTB is true but lucky/unwarranted, so on JTB it is not Knowledge. On a K/B only taxonomy it is also just ‘Belief’, indistinguishable from J¬TB justified false belief and from ¬J¬TB. Truth is invisible once justification fails; a lucky true belief cannot be marked off from a justified false belief or a plain false belief.

Consequences colleagues note for the justification clause when justification must be cashed out in the K/B inventory: justification for p must be supplied by further beliefs or by knowledge. If justification is itself knowledge you get higher-order knowledge requirements and Meno-style regress/circularity; if justification is belief you get belief-justifies-belief. That yields the familiar regress pressure: every justifier needs its own justifier ad infinitum, with no third epistemic status to stop the chain. The only stopping options inside K/B are an infinite hierarchy of justifiers or a dogmatic/foundational base of beliefs taken as justified simply by being believed, i.e. an arbitrary ungrounded terminus, or a collapse of justification into knowledge and circularity.

Hence the common picture is the collapse of the J×T space into K vs Belief, the loss of independent epistemic value for justification apart from truth and for truth apart from justification, and the resulting regress/circularity vs arbitrary foundation pressure for the justification condition. Gettier is explicitly excluded.
reflection_text.6:
The JTB analysis is K = B ∧ T ∧ J with K → B. If the ontology is closed to Knowledge and bare Belief, Belief is the residual ¬K = [J∧¬T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧¬T∧B]. 

That coarse-graining is the core loss that is being reported in round 0. 
* The cell J ∧ ¬T, a justified false belief, is not K because it fails truth. On a K/B only taxonomy it must be called mere Belief, so it is indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief ¬J∧¬T. Justification is therefore invisible once truth fails: a well-supported error cannot be marked as epistemically creditworthy.
* The cell ¬J ∧ T, an unjustified true belief, is not K because it fails justification. On a K/B only taxonomy it must also be called mere Belief, so it is indistinguishable from a justified false belief J∧¬T and from an unjustified false belief. Truth is therefore invisible once justification fails: a lucky true belief cannot be marked as epistemically defective.

Hence Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag of justified/unjustified and true/false states. Knowledge is a proper species of Belief and the distinct normative roles of justification apart from truth and truth apart from justification are lost. This is regularly phrased as justification does not entail truth and truth does not entail justification.

Several colleagues cash this out as the grounding problem for the Justification condition when justification itself must be expressed in the K/B inventory. 
If justification for p is to be a further epistemic state, it must be a piece of Knowledge or a further Belief. 
* Justification as Knowledge gives a higher-order knowledge requirement: to be justified in believing p is to know that p is justified, etc., leading to infinite regress / circularity and Meno’s paradox. 
* Justification as Belief makes justification collapse into further belief, giving an infinite regress of justifiers for justifiers, or if the chain stops, an arbitrary/dogmatic foundation of beliefs taken as basic without themselves being JTB.

Thus the same loss is described both as a taxonomic collapse – justified false belief conflated with unjustified false belief, and unjustified true belief conflated with justified false/unjustified false belief – and as the classic regress vs arbitrary stopping point/dogmatism dilemma for the Justification clause. 

Disagreement in phrasing remains between those who state the problem primarily as the two missing intermediate cells J¬T and ¬J T, and those who state it primarily as regress/circularity versus foundational dogmatism. The two descriptions are compatible, with the regress/dogmatism being the mechanism by which the coarse-graining is forced. Unresolved is which two formulations the questioner wants emphasized, but the consensus on the inventory problem is stable.
reflection_text.11:
The discussion is converging on the coarse-graining that follows from restricting the epistemic inventory to Knowledge and Belief while keeping JTB = B ∧ T ∧ J.

Knowledge is a proper species of belief, K → B, and with only K and B as labels everything that is not JTB has to be filed under the residual ‘Belief’. The 2×2 Truth × Justification space is thus forced into two boxes:

* J T = K
* J ¬T = justified false belief
* ¬J T = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ¬T = unjustified false belief

all map onto B. Belief therefore becomes heterogeneous.

Consensus across the round:

* Loss of a distinct justified-false-belief state. A justified false belief is epistemically good in the sense of justification but not knowledge because it is false. On a K/B only taxonomy it must be called mere Belief, indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief ¬J ¬T. Justification is invisible once truth fails; we lose the ability to mark warranted error as different from unwarranted error.

* Loss of a distinct unjustified-true-belief state. An unjustified true belief is true but not knowledge because it lacks justification. On a K/B only taxonomy it must also be called mere Belief, indistinguishable from a justified false belief J ¬T and from an unjustified false belief. * If justification is cashed in further beliefs, justification requires a further justified belief q, which itself needs justification r, etc. That yields an infinite regress of beliefs-for-justification. Stopping the regress requires a foundational base of beliefs that are taken as justified without further epistemic support, i.e. dogmatic/arbitrary foundationalism. reflection_text.20:
The JTB analysis needs three independent dimensions B, T, J. K = B∧T∧J. With only the two locutions Knowledge and Belief available, everything that is not K is forced into the residual category Belief.

That forces a 2×2 Truth×Justification space into two boxes:
* JT = Knowledge
* J~T = justified false belief
* ~JT = unjustified true belief
* ~J~T = unjustified false belief

are all mapped onto ‘mere Belief’ except the first. Belief is therefore a heterogeneous catch-all K→B. Knowledge is a proper species of belief.

The consensus collapse account from Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,3,4,6,8 is:
1. Justification is lost once truth fails. A justified false belief J∧B∧~T is not K and has no home; it must be called Belief. It is therefore indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief ~J∧B∧~T and from an unjustified true belief. The epistemic credit of a properly supported but false belief is erased; justification cannot be marked as an independent value apart from truth.
2. Truth is lost once justification fails. An unjustified true belief T∧B∧~J is not K and has no home; it must be called Belief. It is therefore indistinguishable from a justified false belief J∧B∧~T and from an unjustified false belief. The epistemic defect of a lucky true belief is erased; truth cannot be marked as an independent value apart from justification. Belief becomes the disjunction of J~T, ~JT and ~J~T.

Several colleagues formalise the loss as regress/circularity/dogmatism for the Justification condition. With only K and B as epistemic resources, a justifier for p must be a belief q or a knowledge k. If it is a belief, q itself needs justification, giving an infinite regress of ever higher order beliefs. The only stops are:
* circularity / bootstrapping: justification is made out of knowledge, i.e. p is justified because it is known, which is circular, or beliefs mutually justify each other;
* arbitrary foundationalism: a base of beliefs is taken as justified simply in virtue of being believed, an ungrounded dogmatic terminus.

Colleagues 2,5,7,9,13,14,16,17,21 present that regress vs arbitrary stopping point as the two pressures generated by the two-state ontology. The regress pressure and the dogmatic foundation pressure are the justificatory expression of the coarse-graining just described: justification cannot be an autonomous epistemic mark because it can only be cashed out in K or B.

Disagreement to track: some colleagues frame the “two problems” as the two non-knowledge cells J~T and ~JT being conflated under Belief; others frame them as infinite regress vs foundational arbitrariness / circularity. Both point to the same underlying loss of an independent justified-belief state and an independent true-belief state once the inventory is restricted to Knowledge and Belief. Unresolved is whether the required answer is expressed as a taxonomic collapse or as a meta-justificatory regress/dogmatism problem; the literature treats them as two sides of the same coarse-graining.

I retain the core claim: with K/B only, JTB cannot keep justified false belief distinct from unjustified false belief and cannot keep unjustified true belief distinct from justified false belief/unjustified false belief, with the attendant regress/circularity/dogmatism consequence for trying to cash justification in terms of K/B alone. Gettier is explicitly excluded.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With JTB as K = B ∧ T ∧ J and K entails B, the only non-knowledge bin you have left is ‘Belief’. That bin is forced to be the logical complement of K, i.e.

B = [J ∧ ¬T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B]

so Belief has to do the work of three distinct epistemic profiles at once. The J × T 2×2 is coarse-grained into two boxes and the two cells that JTB needs to keep visible disappear.

1. Justification is invisible once truth fails. A justified false belief J ∧ B ∧ ¬T is epistemically creditworthy – the belief is properly supported – but on JTB it is not K because it is false. With only K/B available it must be filed as mere Belief, the same label as an unjustified false belief ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T. You lose any distinct state in which a rationally held error can be marked as better than a groundless error. In ordinary terms you cannot keep justified false belief distinct from unjustified false belief; justification ceases to be recognisable as an independent mark of value when the belief turns out false.

2. Truth is invisible once justification fails. An unjustified true belief ¬J ∧ B ∧ T is true in the world but epistemically defective – a lucky guess, a hunch that happens to be right – and on JTB it is not K because it lacks justification. With only K/B available it must also be filed as mere Belief, the same label as a justified false belief J ∧ B ∧ ¬T and as an unjustified false belief. You lose any distinct state in which a lucky true belief can be marked as worse than a justified true belief. Truth ceases to be recognisable as an independent mark of value when justification is absent.

That is why Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag of J¬T, ¬J T and ¬J¬T. The familiar talk of regress or circularity is just the way the coarse-graining shows up when you try to cash out J in terms of K or B: to keep justification visible you would need an intermediate justified-belief state and a distinct true-belief state, and a two-state ontology of Knowledge and Belief simply does not have them.

1.text:
With JTB K = B ∧ T ∧ J and K → B, on a K/B only ontology everything that is
not JTB has to be put in the single residual box B.

The 2×2 T × J space therefore collapses to one marked cell and one
heterogeneous residual:

K = J T B
B∗ = J ¬T B  ∨  ¬J T B  ∨  ¬J ¬T B

Belief is then forced to do the work of three distinct epistemic profiles.

1.  Justification is lost once truth fails: the justified false belief
cell J ¬T B.
A JFB is epistemically creditworthy – it is properly supported – but it
is not K because it is false. On a K/B only inventory it has to be called
mere Belief and is hence indistinguishable from an unjustified false
belief ¬J ¬T B and from an unjustified true belief ¬J T B. There is no
state “justified non-knowledge” in which to house a rationally held false
belief. Justification therefore ceases to be recognisable as an independent
good when truth fails; justification is only ever visible together with
truth, i.e. inside Knowledge. Cashing justification in the only resources
K and B makes justification either knowledge-for-justification,
p justified because it is known to be justified, which is circular/regressive,
or belief-for-justification, p justified because you believe its grounds,
which collapses justification into belief and permits bootstrapping.

2.  Truth is lost once justification fails: the unjustified true belief
cell ¬J T B.
An UTB is true in the world but not K because it is unjustified, e.g. a
lucky guess. On a K/B only inventory it too has to be called mere Belief
and is hence indistinguishable from a justified false belief J ¬T B and
from an unjustified false belief ¬J ¬T B. There is no state “true
non-knowledge” in which to house a lucky true belief. Truth therefore
ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when justification fails;
truth is only ever visible together with justification, i.e. inside
Knowledge. Cashing justification in the only resources K and B then forces
a justificatory chain of beliefs B1, B2 … for p. With no independent
justified-belief state to stop the chain you get either an infinite
regress of justifiers for justifiers, or if the regress is stopped, an
arbitrary, dogmatic foundational base of beliefs taken as justified simply
by being held. In either case the intended distinction between a warranted
true belief, which is Knowledge, and a merely lucky true belief, which is
just Belief, is erased.

Hence Belief becomes a grab-bag of justified falsehood, unjustified
truth and unjustified falsehood. Justification cannot be marked apart from
truth and truth cannot be marked apart from justification once the only
recognised non-knowledge attitude is Belief.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With only Knowledge = JTB and Belief = not-K as the two available locutions, the truth × justification square is forced into two bins.

Knowledge is T J B. Everything else has to be called mere Belief: 

* J ~T = justified false belief
* ~J T = unjustified true belief
* ~J ~T = unjustified false belief

That coarse-graining is the loss.

1. Justification is lost as an independent mark once truth fails. A justified false belief is epistemically creditworthy — it is properly supported, rationally held, a well supported scientific conjecture that happens to be false — but on JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not true. With no distinct justified-belief state, it has to be filed under Belief and is thereby lumped together with an unjustified false belief. There is then no way on a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy to distinguish a rationally held error from an arbitrary error. Justification ceases to be recognizable as a good when truth is absent.

2. Truth is lost as an independent mark once justification fails. An unjustified true belief is true in the world but held by luck, hunch or coincidence — e.g. a lucky guess. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it lacks justification. With only Belief left, it has to be filed under Belief and is thereby lumped together with a justified false belief and with an unjustified false belief. There is then no way to distinguish a lucky true belief from a justified false belief, let alone from a plain false belief. Truth ceases to be recognizable as a good when justification is absent.

Belief therefore becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag of J~T, T~J and ~J~T. K is a proper species of B, and the normative difference between a justified false belief and an unjustified false belief, and the factual difference between an unjustified true belief and a false belief, are erased.

That taxonomic collapse is what drives the familiar regress/circularity talk: once justification has to be expressed in terms of K or B alone, you can either express it in beliefs and get a chain of beliefs about beliefs, or express it in knowledge and get knowledge about knowledge. The regress/circularity is a symptom of the deeper problem that with only Knowledge and Belief we have no independent state in which to house justified non-knowledge and true non-knowledge.

3.text:

it is not knowledge because it is false. With only K/B it has to be called
mere Belief, i.e. it is lumped with ¬J¬T B unjustified false belief and with
¬J T B. There is therefore no epistemic home for a justified but false
belief. Justified false belief is indistinguishable from unjustified false
belief; justification ceases to be recognisable as a good when the belief
turns out false. In justificatory terms this is the demand that a
justifier be itself justified. If justification is cashed out in belief,
p is justified by q, q by r . . . , with no third epistemic status to stop
the chain the account is driven to an infinite regress of justifiers, or to
close the chain.

2. Truth is invisible once justification fails.
¬J T B is true but lucky/unwarranted and on JTB it is not knowledge because
it is not justified. On a K/B only taxonomy it is also just Belief, i.e. it
is lumped with J¬T B justified false belief and with ¬J¬T B. There is
therefore no epistemic home for a true but unwarranted belief. An
unjustified true belief is indistinguishable from a justified false belief
and from a plain false belief; truth ceases to be recognisable as a good
when justification is absent. Closing the justificatory chain inside the
K/B inventory forces a stop.

The only stops available are circularity, knowledge for knowledge, or a
dogmatic foundation. To stop the regress you must posit beliefs that are
treated as justified simply by being believed, or as known in virtue of
being known, i.e. an arbitrary, undefended basic stock of belief on which
knowledge is ultimately grounded, or an outright circular mutual
justification of beliefs. 

That is the coarse-graining: belief becomes the disjunction of justified/
unjustified and true/false, and the classic justification-truth gap
 appears as the inability to mark a justified false belief off from an
unjustified false belief and an unjustified true belief off from a
justified false belief.

With only K and B in the inventory K = B ∧ T ∧ J is a proper species of belief and everything that is not J T B has to be filed under the residual “Belief”.

The Truth × Justification square is then forced into two boxes

* J T = K
* J ¬T , ¬J T , ¬J ¬T → B

Belief is therefore heterogeneous and the independent epistemic values of justification and truth are lost once the other fails.

1. Justification is invisible once truth fails. A justified false belief J ∧ B ∧ ¬T is on JTB not knowledge because it is false, so on a K/B only taxonomy it must be called mere Belief. It is thereby lumped with ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T, an unjustified false belief, and with ¬J ∧ B ∧ T. We lose a distinct epistemically creditworthy non-knowledge state, warranted error. Justification can no longer be marked as an independent good when the belief turns out false.

2. Truth is invisible once justification fails. An unjustified true belief ¬J ∧ B ∧ T is on JTB not knowledge because it is unjustified, so on a K/B only taxonomy it must also be called mere Belief. It is thereby lumped with J ∧ B ∧ ¬T and with ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T. We lose a distinct lucky/accidental true belief state. Truth can no longer be marked as an independent good when justification is absent.

That coarse-graining is the familiar justificatory grounding dilemma in the same language. If justification for p is to be cashed in the only available states, K or B, then justification for p requires a further belief q that justifies p, q itself needs justification r, etc. That is the infinite regress of beliefs-for-justification, or circularity if the chain is closed on itself. The only way to halt the regress inside a K/B inventory is to posit a base of beliefs that are taken as justified without further epistemic support – an arbitrary, dogmatic foundational stop, or to collapse justification into knowledge and make JTB circular. The loss of the J ¬T and ¬J T cells is exactly the formal expression of the regress vs. arbitrary foundation problem.

K = B ∧ T ∧ J

and K → B, a two-state ontology is forced to treat

B = ¬K = [J ∧ ¬T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B]

as a single residual kind.  Belief has to do the work of three
different truth×justification profiles and justification and truth can
only be read off the K/B boundary.

That coarse-graining makes two independently valuable non-knowledge
states disappear.

supported and epistemically creditworthy and still be false. On JTB it
is not K because ¬T so on a Knowledge/Belief only menu it must be
called mere Belief. It is therefore indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B,
unjustified false belief, and from ¬J ∧ T ∧ B. Justification is
invisible once truth fails: there is no epistemic home for warranted
error, and a justified false belief is treated as on a par with an
arbitrary false belief.

2. Unjustified true belief, ¬J ∧ T ∧ B.  A belief can be true in the
world but held by luck, coincidence or wishful thinking. On JTB it is
not K because ¬J so on the binary menu it must again be called mere
Belief. It is therefore indistinguishable from J ∧ ¬T ∧ B,
justified false belief, and from ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. Truth is invisible once
justification fails: there is no epistemic home for lucky truth, and an
unjustified true belief is treated as on a par with a justified false
belief and with an unjustified false belief.

and true/false cases, K is a proper species of B, and the independent
normative roles of justification and of truth are lost. In the grounding
form of the same difficulty this is the familiar justificatory squeeze:
with only K and B to cash out J, justification for p can only be a
further belief q or a piece of knowledge. If it is a belief, p is
justified only if q is justified, q only if r is justified, etc., an
infinite regress of justifiers; if the chain is stopped the only stop
inside the inventory is an unjustified belief taken as basic, i.e. an
arbitrary dogmatic foundation, and if justification is cashed out as

If we really let the epistemic inventory be just Knowledge = JTB and Belief = not-K, the JxT space collapses and Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag. That is where the pressure shows up.

On the ordinary 2 x 2:

JT = Knowledge
J~T = justified false belief
~JT = unjustified true belief
~J~T = unjustified false belief

Knowledge entails Belief, so everything that is not JTB has to be filed as mere Belief. The problem is not Gettier, it is that the two non-knowledge cells that JTB needs to recognise are erased.

1. Justification is lost once truth fails. A justified false belief is epistemically creditworthy even though it is false. On JTB it is not Knowledge because ~T, so with only Knowledge/Belief it must be called mere Belief. That is the same label we must give to an unjustified false belief. We therefore lose any way to mark a rationally held error as epistemically better than a groundless error. Justification ceases to be visible as an independent epistemic value when the belief turns out false.

2. Truth is lost once justification fails. An unjustified true belief is true in the world but epistemically defective, e.g. a lucky guess. On JTB it is not Knowledge because ~J, so with only Knowledge/Belief it must also be called mere Belief. That is the same label we must give to a justified false belief and to an unjustified false belief. We therefore lose any way to mark a lucky true belief as epistemically worse than a warranted true belief, and we cannot keep warranted falsehood apart from accidental truth. Truth ceases to be visible as an independent epistemic value when justification is absent.

Hence Belief is forced to do the work of justified false belief, unjustified true belief and unjustified false belief at once. The two distinct non-knowledge states J~T and ~JT are both unmarkable, so the taxonomy cannot keep justified belief distinct from unjustified belief, nor true belief distinct from false belief, outside the JTB cell. The familiar regress / circularity talk is just the way that loss shows up when you try to cash out justification in terms of the only two kinds you allow: if you try to express J in terms of further Beliefs you get an endless chain, if you try to express J in terms of Knowledge you get circularity. The deeper point is the coarse-graining itself: with only Knowledge and Belief we cannot house a justified but false state and an unjustified but true state, so the independent normative roles of justification and truth are erased.

I think we can get the two pressures more clearly if we stay with the 2×2 Truth × Justification space that JTB is trying to supervise, and ask what a Knowledge/Belief only ontology can still mark.

JTB is K = B & T & J. If the only primitive epistemic labels we allow are Knowledge and mere Belief, then the only cell that gets a name is J T. Everything else — J ¬T, ¬J T, ¬J ¬T — is forced into the single residual box ‘Belief’. Belief therefore has to do the work of three different epistemic profiles, and the normative work of justification and truth gets erased once one of the two conditions fails.

That gives us two distinct losses of discriminatory power, and they are the ones most of us are already pointing to when we talk about the heterogeneous Belief box.

1. Justified false belief is lost as an independent epistemic position. J ¬T is a properly supported, epistemically creditworthy state of error. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not true. With only K / B at our disposal it has to be called mere Belief, and it is therefore lumped together with ¬J ¬T, an unjustified false belief. Justification becomes invisible once truth fails: we have no category in which an agent can be in a good epistemic position with respect to p while p is false. In ordinary talk this is the inability to keep a rationally held false belief distinct from an arbitrary false belief.

2. Unjustified true belief is lost as an independent epistemic position. ¬J T is true in the world but held by luck, accident or wishful thinking. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not justified. With only K / B it too has to be called mere Belief, and it is therefore lumped together with J ¬T and with ¬J ¬T. Truth becomes invisible once justification fails: we have no category in which we can mark a true belief as epistemically defective, i.e. as lucky, as opposed to a justified true belief which we are forced to count as Knowledge. In ordinary talk this is the inability to keep a lucky true belief distinct from a justified false belief, and from a plain false belief.

These are the two coarse-graining problems. The regress / circularity talk that Colleagues 1,10,17,18 are describing is just the way the loss shows up when you try to cash out justification using only the two labels K and B: if justification is made out of Belief you get a regress of beliefs-for-justification, if it is made out of Knowledge you get circularity / bootstrapping. The substantive cost of the two-state inventory, however, is that we can mark JTB as Knowledge but we can no longer keep justified false belief apart from unjustified false belief, nor unjustified true belief apart from justified false belief. Belief becomes the grab-bag of J ¬T, ¬J T and ¬J ¬T, and justification and truth cease to be independently trackable epistemic values.

With only Knowledge = JTB and Belief as the residual non-knowledge category, the two-dimensional space Truth x Justification is forced into a Knowledge/Belief dichotomy and Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag. That coarse-graining is visible in the two cells JTB needs but cannot name.

1. The loss of a justified-but-non-knowledge state. J¬TB is a properly supported belief that happens to be false, e.g. a well-grounded scientific conjecture that turns out false. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it lacks truth, so with only Knowledge and Belief left it must be filed as mere Belief. The same label is then forced on ¬J¬TB, an unjustified false belief. Justification therefore disappears as an independent mark of epistemic value once truth fails: we have no way to mark a justified false belief as epistemically creditworthy non-knowledge distinct from an unjustified false belief. In ordinary talk this is the collapse of justified error into bare belief.

2. The loss of an unjustified-but-true non-knowledge state. T¬JB is a true belief held by luck, a hunch that happens to be right. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it lacks justification, so with only Knowledge and Belief left it must also be filed as mere Belief. That same label is already being used for J¬TB. Truth therefore disappears as an independent mark of epistemic value once justification fails: we have no way to mark an unjustified true belief as lucky non-knowledge distinct from a justified false belief, and indeed distinct from an unjustified false belief. Belief is now simultaneously justified and unjustified, true and false.

Those are the two observable gaps that the regress/circularity formulations are usually meant to capture. Once justification has to be expressed only in terms of Knowledge or in terms of Belief, justification is invisible for false propositions and truth is invisible for unjustified propositions, and the epistemic roles of justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently within a two-state ontology. That is why a distinct justified-belief and a distinct true-belief state are needed if we want to keep J¬TB and ¬JTB apart from ¬J¬TB.

I’m with the regress reading that Colleagues 1, 10, 14, 16 and 21 are developing. With K = JTB and B as the only non-K residue, justification can’t be an independent primitive. If you try to cash justification in epistemic terms you have only two places to put it.

If you try to cash it in Belief, p is justified by a further belief q, q by r, etc. Any belief that is going to do justificatory work has to itself be justified on JTB, so you need a higher-order justifier for the justifier, ad infinitum. That is a genuine infinite regress of beliefs-for-justification, and with no third state such as justified belief there is nothing in the inventory that can stop it in principle.

The second pressure is what the regress forces you to do in practice. You can’t run an infinite chain, so you have to halt it. The only halting move available on a Knowledge/Belief inventory is to treat some beliefs as basic and accept them as justified simply in virtue of being held. Those basic beliefs are not known in the JTB sense – they are not themselves justified by further Knowledge or Belief – so the stopping point is an arbitrary, dogmatic foundation. Knowledge then rests on a base of beliefs that are justified by fiat, not by justification.

What gets described in the literature as “circularity” is just the visible symptom of that coarse-graining. Because the only non-K category is Belief, Belief is forced to be the disjunction

B = [J ∧ ~T ∧ B] ∨ [~J ∧ T ∧ B] ∨ [~J ∧ ~T ∧ B]

i.e. justified false belief, unjustified true belief and unjustified false belief all get lumped together. Justified false belief is epistemically creditworthy but false, so it is not Knowledge; unjustified true belief is true but lucky, so it is not Knowledge. On a two-state taxonomy both are just “Belief”. 

So the operational loss is the loss of independent visibility of justification and truth: we can no longer keep a justified false belief distinct from an unjustified false belief, and we can no longer keep an unjustified true belief distinct from a justified false belief. Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag of the epistemically good, the bad and the merely accidental, and justification is invisible once truth fails while truth is invisible once justification fails. That is the second, and more fundamental, cost of restricting the ontology to Knowledge and Belief, and it is what the regress is driven to in order to avoid circular self-reference.

20.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The JTB analysis needs three independent dimensions B, T, J. K = B∧T∧J, K→B. With only the two locutions Knowledge and Belief available, everything that is not K is forced into the residual category Belief. That forces a 2×2 Truth×Justification space into two boxes:
* JT = Knowledge
* J~T = justified false belief
* ~JT = unjustified true belief
* ~J~T = unjustified false belief are all mapped onto ‘mere Belief’ except the first. Belief is therefore a heterogeneous catch-all K→B. Knowledge is a proper species of belief.

Current round reinforces the consensus collapse account:
1. Justification is lost once truth fails. A justified false belief J∧B∧~T is not K and has no home; it must be called Belief. It is therefore indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief ~J∧B∧~T and from an unjustified true belief ~J∧B∧T. The epistemic credit of a properly supported but false belief is erased; justification cannot be marked as an independent value apart from truth. Cashing justification in K/B makes justification either knowledge-for-justification → circularity/regress, or belief-for-justification → bootstrapping.
2. Truth is lost once justification fails. An unjustified true belief T∧B∧~J is not K and has no home; it must be called Belief. It is therefore indistinguishable from a justified false belief J∧B∧~T and from an unjustified false belief. The epistemic defect of a lucky true belief is erased; truth cannot be marked as an independent value apart from justification. Belief becomes the disjunction of J~T, ~JT and ~J~T.

Formally B = ¬K = [J∧¬T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧¬T∧B]. The loss of the J¬T and ¬JT cells is the discriminatory failure. The familiar regress/circularity/dogmatism formulation is the meta-justificatory expression of the same coarse-graining: with only K and B to cash out J, justification for p must be a belief q or a knowledge k. If belief, q itself needs justification → infinite regress of justifiers. The only stops are circularity/bootstrapping: justification made out of knowledge, p justified because it is known, which is circular; or arbitrary foundationalism/dogmatism: a base of beliefs taken as justified simply in virtue of being believed, an ungrounded terminus.

Disagreement to track remains only verbal: some colleagues frame the “two problems” as the two non-knowledge cells J~T and ~JT being conflated under Belief; others frame them as infinite regress vs foundational arbitrariness/circularity. Multiple colleagues now explicitly link them: the regress vs terminus dilemma is the grounding form of the taxonomic collapse. The substantive cost is the same: no independent state for justified non-knowledge and no independent state for true non-knowledge. Gettier is explicitly excluded.

I retain the core claim: with K/B only, JTB cannot keep justified false belief distinct from unjustified false belief and cannot keep unjustified true belief distinct from justified false belief/unjustified false belief, with the attendant regress/circularity/dogmatism consequence for trying to cash justification in terms of K/B alone. The operational answer is the two coarse-graining losses: justification invisible once truth fails, truth invisible once justification fails.

reflection_text.1:
The JTB analysis is K = B ∧ T ∧ J with K→B. On a K/B-only ontology everything not JTB is forced into a single residual Belief.

B = ¬K = [J∧¬T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧¬T∧B].

Belief therefore has to do the work of three distinct truth × justification profiles and the 2×2 T×J space collapses to one marked cell and one heterogeneous residual.

Consensus taxonomic loss:
1. Justification is lost once truth fails. The J¬T cell, justified false belief, is epistemically creditworthy but false so on JTB it is not K. With only K/B it must be called mere Belief and is indistinguishable from ¬J¬T unjustified false belief and from ¬JT unjustified true belief. There is no state ‘justified non-knowledge’ in which to house warranted error. Justification ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when truth fails; justification is only visible together with truth inside Knowledge.

2. Truth is lost once justification fails. The ¬JT cell, unjustified true belief, is true but epistemically defective, e.g. lucky guess. On JTB it is not K because ¬J. With only K/B it too is mere Belief and is indistinguishable from J¬T justified false belief and from ¬J¬T unjustified false belief. There is no state ‘true non-knowledge’ in which to house lucky truth. Truth ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when justification fails; truth is only visible together with justification inside Knowledge.

These two collapses are the core discriminatory failure: we can mark JTB as Knowledge but cannot keep justified false belief apart from unjustified false belief, nor unjustified true belief apart from justified false belief. Belief becomes a grab-bag of justified/unjustified and true/false.

The same loss is formalised by colleagues as the grounding problem for the justification condition on a K/B inventory. Cashing J in the only resources K or B gives:
* justification as K: to be justified is to know you are justified → regress / circularity K→J→K, Meno’s paradox, bootstrapping.
* justification as B: to be justified is to believe the grounds → regress of beliefs for justification B(p) justified by B(q) justified by B(r)... ad infinitum, with no third epistemic status to stop the chain.

In practice the regress is halted by either an infinite hierarchy, circular mutual support, or an arbitrary foundational/dogmatic base of beliefs taken as justified simply by being held. That is the regress vs. arbitrary foundation / circularity dilemma.

Unresolved framing: colleagues agree on the two missing cells J¬T and ¬JT, but differ in presentation as either the taxonomic collapse itself or as regress/circularity/dogmatism as the structural consequence. Both clusters refer to the same two-state restriction: justification invisible when truth fails, truth invisible when justification fails.
reflection_text.6:
The JTB analysis is K = B ∧ T ∧ J with K → B. On a closed K/B ontology the residual is B = ¬K = [J∧¬T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧¬T∧B]. Belief is therefore the heterogeneous grab-bag of three truth×justification profiles; K is a proper species of Belief and the 2×2 T×J square collapses to K = J T and B* = J ¬T ∨ ¬J T ∨ ¬J ¬T.

The consensus across rounds is that this coarse-graining destroys the independent trackability of justification and truth.

* Justification is invisible once truth fails: the justified false belief cell J∧¬T∧B. It is epistemically creditworthy but not K because ¬T. On K/B only it must be called mere Belief and is indistinguishable from ¬J∧¬T∧B unjustified false belief and from ¬J∧T∧B. There is no state ‘justified non-knowledge’ / ‘warranted error’. Justification can only be marked as a good together with truth, i.e. inside Knowledge.

* Truth is invisible once justification fails: the unjustified true belief cell ¬J∧T∧B. It is true but lucky/defective and not K because ¬J. On K/B only it must also be called mere Belief and is indistinguishable from J∧¬T∧B and ¬J∧¬T∧B. There is no state ‘true non-knowledge’ / ‘lucky truth’. Truth can only be marked as a good together with justification, i.e. inside Knowledge.

Hence Belief simultaneously covers justified falsehood, unjustified truth and unjustified falsehood. The normative difference between justified false belief and unjustified false belief, and between unjustified true belief and false belief, is lost.

This taxonomic loss is regularly described in grounding terms: with only K and B to cash out J, justification for p must be a further K or B. As K it yields higher-order knowledge about justification, know p → know J(p) → ..., i.e. regress/circularity and Meno’s paradox; as B it yields a regress of beliefs-for-justification B(p) justified by B(q) justified by B(r)... ad infinitum. To halt the regress the inventory forces an arbitrary/dogmatic foundational stop – basic beliefs taken as justified simply by being held – or circular mutual justification. Justification = knowledge gives circularity K→J→K; justification = belief gives bootstrapping and infinite regress.

Disagreement in phrasing persists between those who state the problem primarily as the two missing intermediate cells J¬T and ¬JT, and those who state it primarily as regress/circularity vs arbitrary foundation/dogmatism. The two descriptions are compatible, the regress/dogmatism being the mechanism by which the coarse-graining is forced. Unresolved is which pair of formulations the questioner wants emphasized, but the inventory problem – loss of a justified-false-belief home and loss of an unjustified-true-belief home, i.e. justification not entailing truth and truth not entailing justification – is stable.
reflection_text.4:
The JTB analysis needs B,T,J as independent dimensions. With the ontology restricted to Knowledge = JTB and Belief as the sole non-knowledge residue, K→B and Belief is forced to be the disjunction ¬K = [J∧¬T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧¬T∧B]. K marks only the J T cell, everything else is lumped under Belief.

Colleagues in both rounds converge on the same coarse-graining as the substantive loss, phrased in two complementary ways:

* Justification is invisible once truth fails: J∧B∧¬T, justified false belief. On JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬T, so with only K/B it must be called mere Belief. Belief is therefore forced to contain justified states and justified false belief becomes indistinguishable from unjustified false belief ¬J∧¬T∧B and from ¬J∧T∧B. There is no state ‘justified non-knowledge’ in which to house warranted error. Justification ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when truth fails; justification is only visible together with truth inside Knowledge.

* Truth is invisible once justification fails: T∧B∧¬J, unjustified true belief. On JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬J, so with only K/B it must also be called mere Belief. Belief is therefore forced to contain true states and an unjustified lucky true belief becomes indistinguishable from a justified false belief J∧B∧¬T and from an unjustified false belief. There is no state ‘true non-knowledge’ in which to house lucky truth. Truth ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when justification fails; truth is only visible together with justification inside Knowledge.

Hence Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag of J¬T, ¬J T and ¬J¬T, losing the independent normative roles of justification apart from truth and truth apart from justification. That is normally phrased as justification does not entail truth and truth does not entail justification.

The same loss is described by colleagues as the grounding pressure for the Justification condition on a K/B only inventory. With only K and B to cash out J, justification for p must be a Knowledge or a Belief. If it is cashed in Belief, p is justified by q, q by r… an infinite regress of justifiers for justifiers with no independent justified-belief state to stop the chain. If the chain is stopped, the only stop inside the inventory is an unjustified belief taken as basic — an arbitrary dogmatic foundational base — or justification collapses into knowledge, giving circularity K→J→K / bootstrapping. Regress vs arbitrary foundation / circularity is thus the structural consequence of trying to express an independent J condition with only Knowledge and Belief.

Unresolved nuance from earlier rounds remains whether the intended ‘two problems’ are best stated as the two coarse-graining losses J¬T and ¬J T, or as regress vs arbitrary foundation/circularity. Current consensus in round 1 treats them as mutually entailing: the loss of the two intermediate non-knowledge cells is the discriminatory failure, and the regress/circularity/dogmatism dilemma is how that failure shows up when justification is tried to be cashed out in K/B only terms. The two canonical examples colleagues keep returning to are justified false belief and unjustified true belief.
reflection_text.3:
The discussion has converged on the coarse-graining forced by a Knowledge/Belief only ontology under JTB. K = B ∧ T ∧ J and K→B, so ¬K = B is the residual

B = ¬K = [J∧¬T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧¬T∧B].

The 2×2 Truth × Justification space collapses to one marked cell and one heterogeneous residual:

* J T = Knowledge
* J ¬T = justified false belief
* ¬J T = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ¬T = unjustified false belief

All three latter cells are forced into the single label ‘Belief’. Belief therefore has to do the work of three distinct epistemic profiles, K is a proper species of B, and justification and truth can only be read off the K/B boundary.

The two discriminatory losses that are now consistently named are:

1. Justification is invisible / lost once truth fails. J∧B∧¬T is a justified false belief, epistemically creditworthy but not K because ¬T. On K/B only it must be called mere Belief and is indistinguishable from ¬J∧B∧¬T unjustified false belief and from ¬J∧B∧T. There is no state ‘justified non-knowledge’ in which to house warranted error. Justification ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when truth fails; justification is only ever visible together with truth, i.e. inside Knowledge.

2. Truth is invisible / lost once justification fails. ¬J∧B∧T is an unjustified true belief, true in the world but not K because ¬J, e.g. lucky guess. On K/B only it too must be called mere Belief and is indistinguishable from J∧B∧¬T and from ¬J∧B∧¬T. There is no state ‘true non-knowledge’ in which to house lucky truth. Truth ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when justification fails; truth is only ever visible together with justification, i.e. inside Knowledge.

These two collapses are the taxonomic symptom of the grounding pressure that several colleagues describe as regress/terminus. With justification cashable only in K or B, justification of p requires a further belief q or knowledge about p. If in beliefs, p justified by q justified by r… ad infinitum, infinite regress of justifiers with no third epistemic status to stop the chain. If justification is cashed in knowledge, you get circularity/bootstrapping K→J→K. In practice the regress must be stopped, and the only stop inside K/B is an unjustified belief taken as basic: an arbitrary/dogmatic foundation. The familiar formulations – justification invisible when truth fails / truth invisible when justification fails – and the regress/circularity vs arbitrary foundation dilemma are two descriptions of the same loss: no independent epistemic home for a justified but false state and for a true but unjustified state, and Belief becomes a grab-bag of J¬T, ¬JT and ¬J¬T.

Unresolved for the question wording is only terminological: whether to present the problems as the two cell collapses or as regress vs dogmatism/circularity. The literature presents them together, and the current round shows near complete agreement that the substantive cost is the loss of independent tracking of justification and truth outside K.
reflection_text.10:
The JTB restriction to only the epistemic labels Knowledge and Belief forces a 2×2 truth × justification space to collapse into K / ¬K. With K = B ∧ T ∧ J and K→B, everything that is not JTB has to be filed under the residual Belief:

B = ¬K = [J ∧ ¬T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B]

Belief is therefore a heterogeneous grab-bag of justified false belief J¬T, unjustified true belief ¬J T and unjustified false belief ¬J¬T. Knowledge is a proper species of belief.

The consensus across rounds is that this coarse-graining erases two independently valuable non-knowledge profiles.

1. Justification is invisible once truth fails. J ∧ B ∧ ¬T is a justified false belief – properly supported, epistemically creditworthy error. On JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬T, so on a K/B only inventory it must be called mere Belief. It is therefore indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T unjustified false belief and from ¬J ∧ B ∧ T. There is no state ‘justified non-knowledge’ in which to house warranted error. Justification ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when truth fails; justification is only visible together with truth, i.e. inside Knowledge. This is the loss of a distinct epistemically creditworthy non-knowledge state, warranted error conflated with arbitrary error.

2. Truth is invisible once justification fails. ¬J ∧ B ∧ T is an unjustified true belief – true in the world but lucky/unwarranted, e.g. a lucky guess. On JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬J, so on a K/B only inventory it too must be called mere Belief. It is therefore indistinguishable from J ∧ B ∧ ¬T justified false belief and from ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T. There is no state ‘true non-knowledge’ in which to house lucky truth. Truth ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when justification fails; truth is only visible together with justification, i.e. inside Knowledge. This is the loss of a distinct lucky/accidental true belief state, lucky truth conflated with justified falsehood and plain falsehood.

The two losses are often reformulated as the grounding pressure for the Justification condition when justification must be cashed out only in K or B. Cashing J in Belief gives a regress of beliefs-for-justification: p justified by q, q justified by r… ad infinitum with no third epistemic status to stop the chain. Cashing J in Knowledge gives circularity / bootstrapping: p justified because it is known, known because justified. In practice the regress must be halted, and the only halting move inside a K/B inventory is a dogmatic foundational base of beliefs taken as justified simply by being held, or an arbitrary stipulated terminus. The regress/circularity/dogmatism talk is the structural symptom of the taxonomic coarse-graining described in 1 and 2.

No Gettier issues are at stake. The core disagreement is only emphasis: some colleagues present the two problems as discriminatory loss of J¬T and ¬J T; others present them as regress vs arbitrary foundation / circularity. Both describe the same collapse of the truth×justification square into Knowledge vs heterogeneous Belief, with justification and truth no longer independently trackable outside K.
reflection_text.12:
The JTB tripartition needs three independent dimensions B,T,J. With only primitives Knowledge = JTB and Belief, K = B∧T∧J and K→B, so Belief is forced to be the residual ¬K:

B = [J∧¬T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧¬T∧B]

i.e. justified false belief, unjustified true belief and unjustified false belief all share the same label. Belief is a heterogeneous grab-bag and K is a proper species of B.

The consensus across rounds is that this coarse-graining erases two independently valuable non-knowledge cells:

* Justification is invisible once truth fails. J∧¬T∧B is epistemically creditworthy warranted error but on JTB it is not K because ¬T, so on a K/B only inventory it must be called mere Belief and is indistinguishable from ¬J∧¬T∧B unjustified false belief and from ¬J∧T∧B. There is no state “justified non-knowledge”. Justification only shows up together with truth, inside Knowledge.

* Truth is invisible once justification fails. ¬J∧T∧B is true but lucky/unwarranted and on JTB it is not K because ¬J, so on a K/B only inventory it too must be called mere Belief and is indistinguishable from J∧¬T∧B and ¬J∧¬T∧B. There is no state “true non-knowledge”. Truth only shows up together with justification, inside Knowledge.

Hence Belief has to do the work of J¬T, ¬J T and ¬J¬T at once, and the independent normative roles of justification and truth are lost outside K.

Colleagues express the same loss in grounding terms. With only K and B to cash out J, justification for p can only be a further belief q or a piece of knowledge. If belief-for-justification, p justified by q, q by r… you get infinite regress of justifiers; if you stop, the only stop inside K/B is an unjustified belief taken as basic, i.e. arbitrary dogmatic foundationalism. If knowledge-for-justification, you get circularity/bootstrapping K→J→K and Meno regress. Regress vs arbitrary foundation / circularity is the mechanism that makes an independent J state impossible with only K and B.

Remaining nuance: some colleagues state the two problems as the two collapsed cells J¬T and ¬J T, others state them as regress vs terminus/dogmatism vs circularity. The two formulations cohere: the collapse is the taxonomic symptom, regress/circularity/dogmatism is the grounding symptom. No Gettier issues are being considered.
reflection_text.15:
The discussion remains convergent on the coarse-graining forced by restricting the epistemic inventory to Knowledge and Belief only with K = J ∧ T ∧ B and K → B.

On that inventory B := ¬K = [J ∧ ¬T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B]. The Truth × Justification 2×2 collapses to one marked cell JT = K and one heterogeneous residual.

The loss repeatedly flagged in this round is the heterogeneous grab-bag nature of Belief and the loss of independent visibility of justification and truth outside K.

1. Justification is invisible once truth fails. Justified false belief J ∧ B ∧ ¬T is epistemically creditworthy but not K because ¬T. With only K/B it too must be labelled mere Belief and is indistinguishable from J ∧ B ∧ ¬T and from ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T. Belief therefore has to do the work of J¬T, ¬J T and ¬J¬T. K is a proper species of B and the normative differences between justified vs unjustified false belief and between unjustified true belief vs false belief are erased.

Colleagues express the same collapse in grounding language: cashing justification in K or B alone forces either an infinite regress of beliefs-for-justification, circularity/knowledge-for-justification, or an arbitrary dogmatic foundational stop where some beliefs are taken as justified simply by being believed. reflection_text.11:
The K/B only restriction on JTB = B ∧ T ∧ J forces K → B and makes Belief the residual ¬K. The Truth × Justification 2×2 collapses to

* J T B = Knowledge
* J ¬T B ∨ ¬J T B ∨ ¬J ¬T B = Belief

reflection_text.18:
The discussion has stabilised on the coarse-graining that follows from closing the epistemic inventory to K and B with K = JTB and K→B.

With K = B∧T∧J the truth × justification space is 2×2:
J T = K
J ¬T = justified false belief
¬J T = unjustified true belief
¬J ¬T = unjustified false belief

On a K/B only ontology everything ¬K is forced into the single residual label B:
B = ¬K = [J∧¬T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧¬T∧B]
Belief is heterogeneous and has to do the work of three distinct profiles. K is a proper species of B and justification and truth can only be read off the K/B boundary.

The two discriminatory losses that recur across colleagues are:

* Justification is invisible once truth fails. J¬T, a justified false belief, is epistemically creditworthy but not K because ¬T, so on K/B it must be called mere Belief. It is therefore indistinguishable from ¬J¬T, unjustified false belief, and from ¬J T. There is no state “justified non-knowledge”/“warranted error” in which to house a rationally held false belief. Justification ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when truth fails; justification is only visible together with truth inside Knowledge.

* Truth is invisible once justification fails. ¬J T, an unjustified true belief, is true but epistemically defective, e.g. lucky guess, and not K because ¬J, so on K/B it must also be called mere Belief. It is therefore indistinguishable from J¬T and from ¬J¬T. There is no state “true non-knowledge”/“lucky truth” in which to house an unwarranted true belief. Truth ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when justification fails; truth is only visible together with justification inside Knowledge. Hence a justified false belief and an unjustified true belief are lumped together, and both lumped with plain unjustified false belief.

These two collapses are consistently described as the loss of an independent home for justified false belief and for unjustified true belief. 

Many colleagues re-describe the same loss as the classic grounding dilemma for the Justification condition under a two-state ontology: justification for p must be cashed in K or B. If cashed in B, p justified by q, q by r… you get an infinite regress of beliefs-for-justification, or circularity/bootstrapping if closed. If cashed in K you get circularity K→J→K. In practice the regress must be stopped, which on K/B only forces an arbitrary, dogmatic foundational belief taken as justified simply by being held, or a collapse of justification into knowledge. The regress/circularity/dogmatism talk is the formal expression of the taxonomic collapse of J¬T and ¬J T into the heterogeneous residual Belief.

Unresolved nuance remains: some colleagues frame the problem purely as category collapse, others frame it purely as regress vs arbitrary foundation. Both point to the same lack of an independent justified-belief state and independent true-belief state; the taxonomy cannot keep justification and truth as independently trackable values outside the JTB cell. No disagreement on the two cells that disappear, only on emphasis.

Earlier point retained: this is not Gettier. The cost is over-/under-generation of knowledge: justification does not entail truth and truth does not entail justification, so JFB and UTB have no independent home.
reflection_text.8:
The deliberation is now stable on the coarse-graining that follows from JTB = K = B∧T∧J with K→B and only two primitive labels K and B.

On that inventory the truth×justification 2×2 collapses to
* J T B = Knowledge
* B* = ¬K = [J∧¬T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧¬T∧B]

so Belief is forced to do the work of three distinct profiles: justified false belief J¬T, unjustified true belief ¬J T, and unjustised false belief ¬J¬T. K is a proper species of B.

The consensus loss is twofold and is described in round 1 both as taxonomic loss and as the grounding regress/terminus problem.

1. Justification is lost once truth fails – the J¬T cell. A justified false belief is epistemically creditworthy, properly supported though false, but on JTB it is not knowledge because ¬T. With only K/B it must be called mere Belief and is therefore indistinguishable from ¬J¬T unjustified false belief and from ¬J T. There is no state ‘justified non-knowledge’ in which to house warranted error. Justification ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when truth fails; justification is only visible together with truth, i.e. inside Knowledge. Cashing justification in K/B gives the belief-for-justification regress: p justified by q, q by r … or knowledge-for-justification circularity/bootstrapping.

2. Truth is lost once justification fails – the ¬J T cell. An unjustified true belief is true in the world but epistemically defective, lucky/accidental, but on JTB it is not knowledge because ¬J. With only K/B it too must be called mere Belief and is therefore indistinguishable from J¬T justified false belief and ¬J¬T. There is no state ‘true non-knowledge’ in which to house lucky truth. Truth ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when justification fails; truth is only visible together with justification, i.e. inside Knowledge. Cashing justification in K/B forces a justificatory chain B1,B2… with no independent justified-belief stop, giving either an infinite regress of justifiers or, if stopped, an arbitrary dogmatic foundational base of beliefs taken as justified simply by being held, or circularity K→J→K.

Hence Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag of J¬T, ¬J T and ¬J¬T. The two observable gaps are the inability to keep justified false belief distinct from unjustified false belief, and the inability to keep unjustified true belief distinct from justified false belief, i.e. the inability to keep justification and truth as independently trackable epistemic values outside the JTB cell. The regress/circularity/dogmatism formulation is the structural expression of that same coarse-graining.

No Gettier issues are relevant here. The tension in phrasing – taxonomic loss of the two non-knowledge cells vs the classic regress vs arbitrary foundation – remains present in the discussion, but colleagues now treat them as two ways of stating the same structural loss: with no intermediate justified-belief / true-belief state, justification and truth cannot be marked apart from each other on a Knowledge/Belief only ontology.
reflection_text.19:
The discussion has converged on the coarse-graining forced by JTB = B ∧ T ∧ J with the epistemic inventory restricted to Knowledge and Belief, K → B.

K = J ∧ T ∧ B is a proper species of B. The truth×justification square is forced to two boxes:

J T B = K
B∗ = J ¬T B ∨ ¬J T B ∨ ¬J ¬T B

Belief is therefore the residual disjunction of three distinct profiles and is heterogeneous. That loss is described consistently as two independent discriminatory failures, with the regress/circularity/dogmatism talk being the grounding symptom of the same coarse-graining.

1. Justification is invisible once truth fails – the justified false belief cell J ∧ B ∧ ¬T.
A justified but false belief is epistemically creditworthy, warranted error, but on JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬T. With only K/B it must be called mere Belief, so it is lumped with ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T, unjustified false belief, and with ¬J ∧ B ∧ T. There is no state ‘justified non-knowledge’/‘justified belief’ in which to house warranted error. Justification ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when truth fails; justification is only visible together with truth inside Knowledge. Cashing J in K/B alone forces either belief-for-justification with an infinite regress of justifiers B1, B2… or knowledge-for-justification with circularity K → J → K.

2. Truth is invisible once justification fails – the unjustified true belief cell ¬J ∧ B ∧ T.
An unjustified but true belief is true but lucky/accidental, epistemically defective, but on JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬J. With only K/B it too must be called mere Belief, so it is lumped with J ∧ B ∧ ¬T and with ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T. There is no state ‘true non-knowledge’/‘true belief’ in which to house lucky truth. Truth ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when justification fails; truth is only visible together with justification inside Knowledge. The same coarse-graining forces a stop to any justificatory chain: either an infinite regress of beliefs about beliefs, or a dogmatic foundational base of beliefs taken as justified simply by being held, an arbitrary stopping point, or collapse of justification into knowledge.

Hence Belief has to do the work of justified false, unjustified true and unjustified false belief at once. K is a proper species of B, and the independent normative marks of justification and truth are lost outside the JTB cell. The two cells J ¬T and ¬J T are unmarkable: justified false belief is indistinguishable from unjustified false belief, and unjustified true belief is indistinguishable from justified false belief. This is the familiar statement that justification does not entail truth and truth does not entail justification. Most colleagues treat the regress/ circularity/ foundational dogmatism formulation as the structural expression of this taxonomic loss; the substantive problem remains the loss of an independent epistemic home for justified non-knowledge and true non-knowledge. Gettier is explicitly set aside.

reflection_text.20:
The JTB analysis needs three independent dimensions B, T, J. K = B∧T∧J, K→B. With only the two locutions Knowledge and Belief available, everything that is not K is forced into the residual category Belief. That forces a 2×2 Truth×Justification space into two boxes:
* JT = Knowledge
* J~T = justified false belief
* ~JT = unjustified true belief
* ~J~T = unjustified false belief are all mapped onto ‘mere Belief’ except the first. Belief is therefore a heterogeneous catch-all K→B. Knowledge is a proper species of belief.

Current round reinforces the consensus collapse account:
1. Justification is lost once truth fails. A justified false belief J∧B∧~T is not K and has no home; it must be called Belief. It is therefore indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief ~J∧B∧~T and from an unjustified true belief ~J∧B∧T. The epistemic credit of a properly supported but false belief is erased; justification cannot be marked as an independent value apart from truth. Cashing justification in K/B makes justification either knowledge-for-justification → circularity/regress, or belief-for-justification → bootstrapping.
2. Truth is lost once justification fails. An unjustified true belief T∧B∧~J is not K and has no home; it must be called Belief. It is therefore indistinguishable from a justified false belief J∧B∧~T and from an unjustified false belief. The epistemic defect of a lucky true belief is erased; truth cannot be marked as an independent value apart from justification. Belief becomes the disjunction of J~T, ~JT and ~J~T.

Formally B = ¬K = [J∧¬T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧¬T∧B]. The loss of the J¬T and ¬JT cells is the discriminatory failure. The familiar regress/circularity/dogmatism formulation is the meta-justificatory expression of the same coarse-graining: with only K and B to cash out J, justification for p must be a belief q or a knowledge k. If belief, q itself needs justification → infinite regress of justifiers. The only stops are circularity/bootstrapping: justification made out of knowledge, p justified because it is known, which is circular; or arbitrary foundationalism/dogmatism: a base of beliefs taken as justified simply in virtue of being believed, an ungrounded terminus.

Disagreement to track remains only verbal: some colleagues frame the “two problems” as the two non-knowledge cells J~T and ~JT being conflated under Belief; others frame them as infinite regress vs foundational arbitrariness/circularity. Multiple colleagues now explicitly link them: the regress vs terminus dilemma is the grounding form of the taxonomic collapse. The substantive cost is the same: no independent state for justified non-knowledge and no independent state for true non-knowledge. Gettier is explicitly excluded.

I retain the core claim: with K/B only, JTB cannot keep justified false belief distinct from unjustified false belief and cannot keep unjustified true belief distinct from justified false belief/unjustified false belief, with the attendant regress/circularity/dogmatism consequence for trying to cash justification in terms of K/B alone. The operational answer is the two coarse-graining losses: justification invisible once truth fails, truth invisible once justification fails.

Previously incorrect-bloc: 11,12,15,18,19,20,3,4,6,8

* Justification invisible once truth fails = justified false belief J¬T B is lumped with ¬J¬T B and ¬J T B
* Truth invisible once justification fails = unjustified true belief ¬J T B is lumped with J¬T B and ¬J¬T B
