3.text:
With K = B ∧ T ∧ J and K → B the K/B only inventory can mark only the J T B cell.  

¬K = B is the residual

B = ¬K = [J ∧ ¬T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B]

so Belief is forced to do the work of three different truth × justification profiles and K is a proper species of B. The 2×2 T × J is coarse-grained to

* J T = Knowledge
* J ¬T, ¬J T, ¬J ¬T → mere Belief

That coarse-graining erases two independently intelligible non-knowledge states.

1. Justification is invisible once truth fails. J ∧ B ∧ ¬T is a justified false belief, properly supported and epistemically creditworthy, but on JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬T. On a K/B only taxonomy it must be called mere Belief and is therefore indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T unjustified false belief and from ¬J ∧ B ∧ T. There is no state ‘justified non-knowledge’ in which to house warranted error. Justification ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when truth fails; justification is only ever visible together with truth, i.e. inside Knowledge.

2. Truth is invisible once justification fails. ¬J ∧ B ∧ T is an unjustified true belief, true in the world but held by luck/accident, and on JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬J. On a K/B only taxonomy it too must be called mere Belief and is therefore indistinguishable from J ∧ B ∧ ¬T justified false belief and from ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T. There is no state ‘true non-knowledge’ in which to house lucky truth. Truth ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when justification fails; truth is only ever visible together with justification, i.e. inside Knowledge.

Hence Belief becomes the heterogeneous grab-bag J¬T ∨ ¬J T ∨ ¬J¬T. The loss of the J¬T and ¬J T cells is the taxonomic form of the familiar grounding pressure: cashing J in K or B alone gives an infinite regress of justifiers, circularity K → J → K, or, to stop the regress, an arbitrary dogmatic foundational base of beliefs taken as justified simply by being held.

4.text:
With JTB  K = B ∧ T ∧ J and on a K/B only inventory K → B so

B = ¬K = [J ∧ B ∧ ¬T] ∨ [¬J ∧ B ∧ T] ∨ [¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T]

i.e. J T is marked as Knowledge and the three other cells of the
truth × justification square are forced into the single residual
‘Belief’. Belief is therefore heterogeneous and justification and truth
can only be read off the K/B boundary.

1. Justification is invisible once truth fails. 
J ∧ B ∧ ¬T is a justified false belief. It is epistemically creditworthy,
properly supported warranted error, but on JTB it is not Knowledge because
¬T. With only K/B it must be called mere Belief and is thereby lumped
with ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T, an unjustified false belief, and with ¬J ∧ B ∧ T.
There is no state ‘justified non-knowledge’ in which to house warranted
error. Justification can no longer be marked as an independent good when
the belief turns out false; justification is only ever visible together
with truth inside Knowledge. In grounding terms this is the demand that a
justifier be itself justified and with no independent justified-belief
state to stop the chain you get an infinite regress of beliefs-for-
justification, or, if the chain is stopped, a dogmatic foundational base
taken as justified simply by being held, and if justification is cashed
out as knowledge you get K → J → K circularity/bootstrapping.

2. Truth is invisible once justification fails. 
¬J ∧ B ∧ T is an unjustified true belief. It is true in the world but
held by luck/accident and on JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬J. With
only K/B it too must be called mere Belief and is thereby lumped with

state ‘true non-knowledge’ in which to house lucky truth. Truth can no
longer be marked as an independent good when justification is absent;
truth is only ever visible together with justification inside Knowledge.
In grounding terms this is the need for a stopping point for the
justificatory chain inside a K/B inventory: the only stops available are
an arbitrary, undefended basic stock of belief taken as justified by fiat,
or a collapse of justification into knowledge.

Hence Belief becomes the grab-bag J¬T, ¬J T and ¬J¬T. K is a proper species
of B and the taxonomy cannot keep a justified false belief distinct from
an unjustified false belief, nor an unjustified true belief distinct from
a justified false belief. Justification does not entail truth and truth
does not entail justification, so the independent normative roles of
justification apart from truth and truth apart from justification are lost
outside the J T cell.

With only K/B it must be called mere Belief and is thereby lumped with ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T, unjustified false belief, and with ¬J ∧ B ∧ T. There is no state ‘justified non-knowledge’/‘justified belief’ in which to house warranted error. Justification therefore ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when truth fails; justification is only ever visible together with truth, i.e. inside Knowledge. Cashing J in K/B alone forces justification to be a further belief q for p, q for r… or knowledge for knowledge, i.e. the familiar regress/circularity pressure.

2. Truth is invisible once justification fails. ¬J ∧ B ∧ T is an unjustified true belief. It is true but lucky/accidental, epistemically defective, but on JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬J. Hence Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag of J¬T, ¬JT and ¬J¬T. K is a proper species of B and the independent normative marks of justification and truth are lost outside the JTB cell. Justified false belief is indistinguishable from unjustified false belief and unjustified true belief is indistinguishable from justified false belief. That is the inability to mark a warranted error apart from a groundless error and a lucky true belief apart from a warranted false belief on a Knowledge/Belief only ontology.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think we’re converging on exactly the same pressure, just under two descriptions. Colleagues 1,10,17,18 are right that cashing justification out with only Knowledge and Belief at our disposal forces a justificatory chain that either never terminates or folds back on itself, and that’s the familiar regress/circularity picture. Colleagues 11,12,13,14,15,16,4,8,19,20 are describing what that pressure is in taxonomic terms, and that’s the way I find it most perspicuous.

With K = B ∧ T ∧ J and K → B the only cell that gets a name is JT. Everything else is forced into the residual B = ¬K:

B = [J∧¬T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧¬T∧B]

Belief is therefore a heterogeneous catch-all and justification and truth can only be read off together inside Knowledge.

On JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬T, so on a K/B only inventory it must be called mere Belief. That is the same label we are forced to give to ¬J¬T B unjustified false belief and to ¬J T B. There is no epistemic home for “justified non-knowledge”. A well-supported scientific conjecture that turns out false is lumped with an arbitrary false belief, and justification ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when the belief is false. In grounding language this is the demand for a justifier for the justifier, which with only B and K to work with becomes an infinite regress of beliefs-for-justification, or if you try to cash justification in Knowledge, knowledge-for-knowledge.

2. Truth is invisible once justification fails. ¬J T B is an unjustified true belief, a lucky guess. On JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬J, so it too must be called mere Belief. That is the same label we are forced to give to J¬T B. There is no epistemic home for “true non-knowledge”. A lucky true belief is lumped with a justified false belief and with an unjustified false belief, and truth ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when justification is absent. In grounding language this is the need for a stopping point: the regress can only be halted by positing a base of beliefs taken as justified simply by being held, an arbitrary dogmatic foundation, or by collapsing justification into knowledge, i.e. circularity/bootstrapping.

So the two problems are really the two unmarkable non-knowledge states that a K/B only ontology erases: we cannot keep a justified false belief distinct from an unjustified false belief, and we cannot keep an unjustified true belief distinct from a justified false belief. K is a proper species of B and Belief becomes the grab-bag of J¬T, ¬J T and ¬J¬T. The regress/circularity formulation is the formal way that coarse-graining shows up when you try to express J using only K and B, but the substantive cost is the loss of independent visibility of justification apart from truth and truth apart from justification.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The JTB restriction to only the epistemic labels Knowledge and Belief forces a 2×2 truth × justification space to collapse into K / ¬K. With K = B ∧ T ∧ J and K → B, everything that is not JTB has to be filed under the residual Belief:

B = ¬K = [J ∧ ¬T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B]

Belief is therefore a heterogeneous grab-bag of justified false belief J¬T, unjustified true belief ¬J T and unjustified false belief ¬J¬T. Knowledge is a proper species of belief.

The consensus across rounds is that this coarse-graining erases two independently valuable non-knowledge profiles.

1. Justification is invisible once truth fails. J ∧ B ∧ ¬T is a justified false belief – properly supported, epistemically creditworthy error. On JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬T, so on a K/B only inventory it must be called mere Belief. It is therefore indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T unjustified false belief and from ¬J ∧ B ∧ T. There is no state ‘justified non-knowledge’ in which to house warranted error. Justification ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when truth fails; justification is only visible together with truth, i.e. inside Knowledge. This is the loss of a distinct epistemically creditworthy non-knowledge state, warranted error conflated with arbitrary error.

2. Truth is invisible once justification fails. ¬J ∧ B ∧ T is an unjustified true belief – true in the world but lucky/unwarranted, e.g. a lucky guess. On JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬J, so on a K/B only inventory it too must be called mere Belief. It is therefore indistinguishable from J ∧ B ∧ ¬T justified false belief and from ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T. There is no state ‘true non-knowledge’ in which to house lucky truth. Truth ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when justification fails; truth is only visible together with justification, i.e. inside Knowledge. This is the loss of a distinct lucky/accidental true belief state, lucky truth conflated with justified falsehood and plain falsehood.

The two losses are often reformulated as the grounding pressure for the Justification condition when justification must be cashed out only in K or B. Cashing J in Belief gives a regress of beliefs-for-justification: p justified by q, q justified by r… ad infinitum with no third epistemic status to stop the chain. Cashing J in Knowledge gives circularity / bootstrapping: p justified because it is known, known because justified. In practice the regress must be halted, and the only halting move inside a K/B inventory is a dogmatic foundational base of beliefs taken as justified simply by being held, or an arbitrary stipulated terminus. The regress/circularity/dogmatism talk is the structural symptom of the taxonomic coarse-graining described in 1 and 2.

No Gettier issues are at stake. The core disagreement is only emphasis: some colleagues present the two problems as discriminatory loss of J¬T and ¬J T; others present them as regress vs arbitrary foundation / circularity. Both describe the same collapse of the truth×justification square into Knowledge vs heterogeneous Belief, with justification and truth no longer independently trackable outside K.

The discussion has converged on the coarse-graining forced by a Knowledge/Belief only ontology under JTB. K = B ∧ T ∧ J and K→B, so ¬K = B is the residual

B = ¬K = [J∧¬T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧¬T∧B].

The 2×2 Truth × Justification space collapses to one marked cell and one heterogeneous residual:

* J T = Knowledge
* J ¬T = justified false belief
* ¬J T = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ¬T = unjustified false belief

All three latter cells are forced into the single label ‘Belief’. Belief therefore has to do the work of three distinct epistemic profiles, K is a proper species of B, and justification and truth can only be read off the K/B boundary.

The two discriminatory losses that are now consistently named are:

1. Justification is invisible / lost once truth fails. J∧B∧¬T is a justified false belief, epistemically creditworthy but not K because ¬T. On K/B only it must be called mere Belief and is indistinguishable from ¬J∧B∧¬T unjustified false belief and from ¬J∧B∧T. There is no state ‘justified non-knowledge’ in which to house warranted error. Justification ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when truth fails; justification is only ever visible together with truth, i.e. inside Knowledge.

2. Truth is invisible / lost once justification fails. ¬J∧B∧T is an unjustified true belief, true in the world but not K because ¬J, e.g. lucky guess. On K/B only it too must be called mere Belief and is indistinguishable from J∧B∧¬T and from ¬J∧B∧¬T. There is no state ‘true non-knowledge’ in which to house lucky truth. Truth ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when justification fails; truth is only ever visible together with justification, i.e. inside Knowledge.

These two collapses are the taxonomic symptom of the grounding pressure that several colleagues describe as regress/terminus. With justification cashable only in K or B, justification of p requires a further belief q or knowledge about p. If in beliefs, p justified by q justified by r… ad infinitum, infinite regress of justifiers with no third epistemic status to stop the chain. If justification is cashed in knowledge, you get circularity/bootstrapping K→J→K. In practice the regress must be stopped, and the only stop inside K/B is an unjustified belief taken as basic: an arbitrary/dogmatic foundation. The familiar formulations – justification invisible when truth fails / truth invisible when justification fails – and the regress/circularity vs arbitrary foundation dilemma are two descriptions of the same loss: no independent epistemic home for a justified but false state and for a true but unjustified state, and Belief becomes a grab-bag of J¬T, ¬JT and ¬J¬T.

Unresolved for the question wording is only terminological: whether to present the problems as the two cell collapses or as regress vs dogmatism/circularity. The literature presents them together, and the current round shows near complete agreement that the substantive cost is the loss of independent tracking of justification and truth outside K. No substantive disagreement remains; earlier mis-labelling of cells has been corrected.

reflection_text.8:
The deliberation has stabilized on the coarse-graining implied by JTB = K = B∧T∧J with K→B and only the two primitive labels K and B.

On that inventory the truth × justification 2×2 collapses to
* J T B = Knowledge
* B* = ¬K = [J∧¬T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧¬T∧B]
so Belief is forced to do the work of three distinct profiles: justified false belief J¬T, unjustified true belief ¬J T, and unjustified false belief ¬J¬T. K is a proper species of B.

Consensus loss is twofold and is now described uniformly as taxonomic loss with the regress/circularity/dogmatism formulation as its grounding symptom.

1. Justification is invisible once truth fails – the J¬T cell. A justified false belief is epistemically creditworthy, properly supported though false, but on JTB it is not knowledge because ¬T. With only K/B it must be called mere Belief and is therefore indistinguishable from ¬J¬T unjustified false belief and from ¬J T. There is no state ‘justified non-knowledge’ in which to house warranted error. Justification ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when truth fails; justification is only visible together with truth, i.e. inside Knowledge. Cashing justification in K/B gives the belief-for-justification regress p justified by q, q by r … with no third epistemic status to stop the chain, or collapse to K→J→K circularity/bootstrapping.

2. Truth is invisible once justification fails – the ¬J T cell. An unjustified true belief is true in the world but epistemically defective, lucky/accidental, but on JTB it is not knowledge because ¬J. With only K/B it too must be called mere Belief and is therefore indistinguishable from J¬T justified false belief and ¬J¬T. There is no state ‘true non-knowledge’ in which to house lucky truth. Truth ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when justification fails; truth is only visible together with justification, i.e. inside Knowledge. Cashing justification in K/B forces a justificatory chain B1,B2… with no independent justified-belief stop, giving either an infinite regress of justifiers or, if stopped, an arbitrary dogmatic foundational base of beliefs taken as justified simply by being held, or circularity.

Hence Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag of J¬T, ¬J T and ¬J¬T. The two observable gaps are the inability to keep justified false belief distinct from unjustified false belief, and the inability to keep unjustified true belief distinct from justified false belief, i.e. the inability to keep justification and truth as independently trackable epistemic values outside the JTB cell. The regress/circularity/dogmatism formulation is the structural expression of that same coarse-graining.

No Gettier issues are relevant. The earlier tension in phrasing – taxonomic loss of the two non-knowledge cells vs classic regress vs arbitrary foundation – remains present in the discussion but colleagues now treat them as two ways of stating the same structural loss: with no intermediate justified-belief / true-belief state, justification and truth cannot be marked apart from each other on a Knowledge/Belief only ontology.
reflection_text.11:
With the JTB analysis K = B ∧ T ∧ J and K → B, a Knowledge/Belief only inventory can name only the JT cell. The residual is B = ¬K = [J ∧ ¬T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B], so the Truth × Justification 2×2 collapses to JT = Knowledge and J¬T, ¬J T, ¬J¬T → mere Belief. Belief is therefore a heterogeneous grab-bag and K is a proper species of B; justification and truth can only be read off together inside K.

The convergent taxonomic loss that rounds 1-2 keep stating is two-fold:

1. Justification is invisible once truth fails / loss of a justified-but-non-knowledge state. J ¬T B is a justified false belief, properly supported warranted error. On JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬T, so on a K/B inventory it must be labelled mere Belief and is lumped with ¬J ¬T B unjustified false belief and with ¬J T B. There is no state “justified non-knowledge” in which to house warranted error. Justification ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when the belief turns out false. In grounding terms this is cashing J in B only: p justified by q, q by r… with no third epistemic status to stop the chain, i.e. infinite regress of beliefs-for-justification or, if J is cashed in K, circularity K → J → K/bootstrapping.

2. Truth is invisible once justification fails / loss of a true-but-non-knowledge state. ¬J T B is an unjustified true belief, true in the world but held by luck/accident. On JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬J, so on a K/B inventory it too must be labelled mere Belief and is lumped with J ¬T B and ¬J ¬T B. There is no state “true non-knowledge” in which to house lucky truth. Truth ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when justification is absent. In grounding terms this is the need for a stopping point inside K/B: the regress can only be halted by an arbitrary dogmatic foundational base of beliefs taken as justified simply by being held, or by collapsing justification into knowledge.

Hence Belief does the work of J¬T, ¬J T and ¬J¬T at once. We can still mark JTB as Knowledge but we cannot keep a justified false belief distinct from an unjustified false belief, nor an unjustified true belief distinct from a justified false belief. The familiar regress/circularity/dogmatism formulation is the dynamic/grounding expression of the same static coarse-graining: cashing justification out with only K and B forces either an endless chain of beliefs-for-justification, a circular knowledge-for-justification, or an undefended foundational stop.

Colleagues 1,10,17,21 continue to phrase the pressure as regress vs circularity/arbitrary foundation; Colleagues 11,12,14,15,16,18,19,20,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,21 now describe it predominantly as the discriminatory loss of the J¬T and ¬J T cells. Round 2 shows the two descriptions are being used interchangeably as taxonomic loss vs its grounding symptom. No Gettier issues are in play. The core taxonomy and the two-cell loss remain stable; the unresolved nuance from earlier rounds about which wording is “the” intended formulation persists only as a terminological mapping, not as substantive disagreement.
reflection_text.10:
The JTB restriction to only the epistemic labels Knowledge and Belief forces a 2×2 truth × justification space to collapse into K / ¬K. With K = B ∧ T ∧ J and K → B, everything that is not JTB has to be filed under the residual Belief:

B = ¬K = [J ∧ ¬T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B]

Belief is therefore a heterogeneous grab-bag of justified false belief J¬T, unjustified true belief ¬J T and unjustified false belief ¬J¬T. Knowledge is a proper species of belief.

The consensus across rounds is that this coarse-graining erases two independently valuable non-knowledge profiles.

1. Justification is invisible once truth fails. J ∧ B ∧ ¬T is a justified false belief – properly supported, epistemically creditworthy error. On JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬T, so on a K/B only inventory it must be called mere Belief. It is therefore indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T unjustified false belief and from ¬J ∧ B ∧ T. There is no state ‘justified non-knowledge’ in which to house warranted error. Justification ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when truth fails; justification is only visible together with truth, i.e. inside Knowledge. This is the loss of a distinct epistemically creditworthy non-knowledge state, warranted error conflated with arbitrary error.

2. Truth is invisible once justification fails. ¬J ∧ B ∧ T is an unjustified true belief – true in the world but lucky/unwarranted, e.g. a lucky guess. On JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬J, so on a K/B only inventory it too must be called mere Belief. It is therefore indistinguishable from J ∧ B ∧ ¬T justified false belief and from ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T. There is no state ‘true non-knowledge’ in which to house lucky truth. Truth ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when justification fails; truth is only visible together with justification, i.e. inside Knowledge. This is the loss of a distinct lucky/accidental true belief state, lucky truth conflated with justified falsehood and plain falsehood.

The two losses are often reformulated as the grounding pressure for the Justification condition when justification must be cashed out only in K or B. Cashing J in Belief gives a regress of beliefs-for-justification: p justified by q, q justified by r… ad infinitum with no third epistemic status to stop the chain. Cashing J in Knowledge gives circularity / bootstrapping: p justified because it is known, known because justified. In practice the regress must be halted, and the only halting move inside a K/B inventory is a dogmatic foundational base of beliefs taken as justified simply by being held, or an arbitrary stipulated terminus. The regress/circularity/dogmatism talk is the structural symptom of the taxonomic coarse-graining described in 1 and 2.

No Gettier issues are at stake. The core disagreement is only emphasis: some colleagues present the two problems as discriminatory loss of J¬T and ¬J T; others present them as regress vs arbitrary foundation / circularity. Both describe the same collapse of the truth×justification square into Knowledge vs heterogeneous Belief, with justification and truth no longer independently trackable outside K.

reflection_text.12:
The JTB tripartition needs three independent dimensions B,T,J. With only primitives Knowledge = JTB and Belief, K = B∧T∧J and K→B, so Belief is forced to be the residual ¬K:

B = [J∧¬T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧T∧B] ∨ [¬J∧¬T∧B]

i.e. justified false belief, unjustified true belief and unjustified false belief all share the same label. Belief is a heterogeneous grab-bag and K is a proper species of B.

The consensus across rounds is now unanimous that this coarse-graining erases two independently valuable non-knowledge cells:

* Justification is invisible once truth fails. J∧¬T∧B is epistemically creditworthy warranted error but on JTB it is not K because ¬T, so on a K/B only inventory it must be called mere Belief and is indistinguishable from ¬J∧¬T∧B unjustified false belief and from ¬J∧T∧B. There is no state “justified non-knowledge”. Justification only shows up together with truth, inside Knowledge. In grounding terms this is the demand that a justifier be itself justified: cashing J in Belief gives p justified by q, q by r… and with no third epistemic status to stop the chain you get an infinite regress of beliefs-for-justification or a collapse to K→J→K circularity/bootstrapping.

* Truth is invisible once justification fails. ¬J∧T∧B is true but lucky/unwarranted and on JTB it is not K because ¬J, so on a K/B only inventory it too must be called mere Belief and is indistinguishable from J∧¬T∧B and ¬J∧¬T∧B. There is no state “true non-knowledge”. Truth only shows up together with justification, inside Knowledge. In grounding terms this is the need for a stopping point: the regress can only be halted inside K/B by a dogmatic foundational base of beliefs taken as justified simply by being held, or by circular bootstrapping K→J→K.

Hence Belief has to do the work of J¬T, ¬J T and ¬J¬T at once, and the independent normative roles of justification and truth are lost outside K.

Colleagues express the same loss in grounding terms. With only K and B to cash out J, justification for p can only be a further belief q or a piece of knowledge. If belief-for-justification, p justified by q, q by r… you get infinite regress of justifiers; if you stop, the only stop inside K/B is an unjustified belief taken as basic, i.e. arbitrary dogmatic foundationalism. If knowledge-for-justification, you get circularity/bootstrapping K→J→K and Meno regress. Regress vs arbitrary foundation / circularity is the mechanism that makes an independent J state impossible with only K and B.

Remaining nuance: some colleagues state the two problems as the two collapsed cells J¬T and ¬J T, others state them as regress vs terminus/dogmatism vs circularity. The two formulations cohere: the collapse is the taxonomic symptom, regress/circularity/dogmatism is the grounding symptom. No Gettier issues are being considered. Round 2 shows full convergence on the taxonomic description of justification-invisible-when-false and truth-invisible-when-unjustified, with Belief = ¬K = J¬T ∨ ¬JT ∨ ¬J¬T as the formal expression.

K is a proper species of B and J and T are only independently readable together inside K.

Current round consensus:

1. Justification is invisible once truth fails. J ∧ B ∧ ¬T = justified false belief is properly supported/warranted error, epistemically creditworthy but not K because ¬T. On K/B only it must be labelled mere Belief and is indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T unjustified false belief and from ¬J ∧ B ∧ T. There is no state ‘justified non-knowledge’/justified belief in which to house warranted error. Justification ceases to be an independent good when truth fails; a justified false belief is treated on a par with unjustified false belief. In grounding terms this is cashing J in B : p justified by q, q by r… with no third epistemic status to stop the chain → infinite regress of beliefs-for-justification, or collapse to K→J→K circularity/bootstrapping.

2. Truth is invisible once justification fails. ¬J ∧ B ∧ T = unjustified true belief is true but lucky/unwarranted, epistemically defective but not K because ¬J. On K/B only it must also be labelled mere Belief and is indistinguishable from J ∧ B ∧ ¬T and from ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T. There is no state ‘true non-knowledge’/true belief in which to house lucky truth. Truth ceases to be an independent good when justification fails; an unjustified true belief is treated on a par with a justified false belief and plain false belief. In grounding terms this is the need for a stopping point inside K/B: infinite regress, or if halted, an arbitrary dogmatic foundational base of beliefs taken as justified simply by being held, or circular collapse J→K→J.

Hence Belief is a heterogeneous grab-bag J¬T ∨ ¬JT ∨ ¬J¬T. JTB can still mark JTB as Knowledge but cannot keep a justified false belief distinct from an unjustified false belief, nor an unjustified true belief distinct from a justified false belief. Justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently outside K.

Previously unresolved phrasing is now essentially resolved: the substantive content is the discriminatory failures J¬T conflation and ¬JT conflation. There is no state “true non-knowledge”/lucky truth in which an unwarranted true belief can be housed. Truth ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when justification fails; truth is only visible together with justification inside Knowledge.

reflection_text.19:
The JTB analysis with an inventory restricted to Knowledge and Belief forces a coarse-graining of the Truth × Justification 2×2.

K = B ∧ T ∧ J and K → B. The only nameable cell is J T B = Knowledge. The residual is

B = ¬K = [J ∧ ¬T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B]

so Belief is a heterogeneous grab-bag of three distinct profiles and K is a proper species of B. Justification and truth can only be read off together inside K.

Two independent discriminatory losses follow, which colleagues now describe consistently as a taxonomic collapse whose grounding symptom is the regress/circularity/dogmatism dilemma.

1. Justification is invisible once truth fails. J ∧ B ∧ ¬T is a justified false belief: properly supported, epistemically creditworthy warranted error. On JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬T, so on a K/B only taxonomy it must be called mere Belief. It is then indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T unjustified false belief and from ¬J ∧ B ∧ T. There is no state ‘justified non-knowledge’/‘justified belief’ in which to house warranted error. Justification ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when truth fails; justification is only visible together with truth inside Knowledge. Cashing J in K/B alone forces p justified by belief q, q by r… or justification collapsed into knowledge, i.e. infinite regress of beliefs-for-justification or K → J → K circularity/bootstrapping.

2. Truth is invisible once justification fails. ¬J ∧ B ∧ T is an unjustified true belief: true in the world but lucky/accidental, epistemically defective. On JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬J, so on a K/B only taxonomy it too must be called mere Belief. It is then indistinguishable from J ∧ B ∧ ¬T justified false belief and from ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T. There is no state ‘true non-knowledge’/‘true belief’ in which to house lucky truth. Truth ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when justification fails; truth is only visible together with justification inside Knowledge. Inside K/B this forces a stopping point for the justificatory chain: either an infinite regress of justifiers, or an arbitrary dogmatic foundational base of beliefs taken as justified simply by being held, or a collapse of justification into knowledge.

Hence Belief must do the work of J¬T, ¬JT and ¬J¬T at once. JTB can mark JTB as Knowledge but cannot keep a justified false belief distinct from an unjustified false belief, nor an unjustified true belief distinct from a justified false belief. The independent normative marks of justification apart from truth and truth apart from justification are lost outside the JTB cell. Gettier is set aside. * J ¬T B , ¬J T B , ¬J ¬T B → mere Belief

Belief is a heterogeneous grab-bag, K is a proper species of B, and J and T can only be read off together inside the JTB cell.

The two substantive losses that are now consistently named across rounds 1-3 are:

1. Justification is invisible once truth fails / no home for justified non-knowledge. J ∧ B ∧ ¬T is a justified false belief, properly supported warranted error, epistemically creditworthy although ¬T so not K on JTB. On K/B only it must be called mere Belief and is indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T unjustified false belief and from ¬J ∧ B ∧ T. There is no state ‘justified non-knowledge’. Justification ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when truth fails; justification is only visible together with truth inside Knowledge. In grounding terms this is the demand that a justifier be itself justified: cashing J in K/B gives p justified by q, q by r… with no third epistemic status to stop the chain.

2. Truth is invisible once justification fails / no home for true non-knowledge. ¬J ∧ B ∧ T is an unjustified true belief, true in the world but lucky/accidental, epistemically defective so ¬J so not K. On K/B only it too must be called mere Belief and is indistinguishable from J ∧ B ∧ ¬T and from ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T. There is no state ‘true non-knowledge’. Truth ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when justification is absent; truth is only visible together with justification inside Knowledge. In grounding terms this is the need for a stopping point for the justificatory chain inside K/B: infinite regress of beliefs-for-justification, circular collapse K→J→K / bootstrapping, or an arbitrary dogmatic foundational base of beliefs taken as justified simply by being held.

Hence Belief is forced to do the work of J¬T ∨ ¬J T ∨ ¬J¬T. JTB can still mark JTB as Knowledge, but it cannot keep a justified false belief distinct from an unjustified false belief, nor an unjustified true belief distinct from a justified false belief. The independent normative roles of justification apart from truth and truth apart from justification are erased outside the JTB cell.

The regress / circularity / dogmatism formulation that several colleagues originally raised is now understood as the dynamic grounding symptom of this static taxonomic loss: without an independent justified-belief state and an independent true-belief state, justification cannot be cashed out with only K and B resources without regress, circularity or an arbitrary foundational stop. No substantive disagreement remains in round 3; earlier mis-labelling of cells has been corrected and the group converges on the two cell losses as the core problems, with terminological variation only about whether to present them as the two collapses or as regress vs dogmatism/circularity.

1.text:
With K = B ∧ T ∧ J and K → B a Knowledge / Belief only inventory can name only the JT cell.

B = ¬K = [J ∧ ¬T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B]

so the Truth × Justification 2×2 is coarse-grained to JT = Knowledge and J¬T ∨ ¬JT ∨ ¬J¬T = mere Belief. K is a proper species of B and J and T can only be read off together inside K.

That coarse-graining erases two independently markable non-knowledge profiles.

1. Justification is invisible once truth fails. J ∧ B ∧ ¬T is a justified false belief, properly supported warranted error, epistemically creditworthy although false. On JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬T, so on a K/B menu it must be called mere Belief. It is then indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T unjustified false belief and from ¬J ∧ B ∧ T unjustified true belief. There is no state ‘justified non-knowledge’ in which to house warranted error. Justification ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when the belief turns out false; a well supported false belief is lumped with an arbitrary false belief. Cashed out in K/B this is the demand that a justifier be itself justified: p justified by q, q by r… with no third epistemic status to stop the chain you get infinite regress of beliefs-for-justification or collapse to K → J → K circularity/bootstrapping.

2. Truth is invisible once justification fails. ¬J ∧ B ∧ T is an unjustified true belief, true in the world but lucky/accidental, epistemically defective. On JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬J, so on the same binary menu it too must be called mere Belief. It is then indistinguishable from J ∧ B ∧ ¬T justified false belief and from ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T. There is no state ‘true non-knowledge’ in which to house lucky truth. Truth ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when justification is absent; a lucky true belief is lumped with a justified false belief and with plain false belief. Cashed out in K/B this is the need for a stopping point for the justificatory chain: the regress can only be halted by a dogmatic foundational base of beliefs taken as justified simply by being held, or by circular bootstrapping.

Hence Belief is the heterogeneous grab-bag J¬T ∨ ¬JT ∨ ¬J¬T. JTB can still mark JTB as Knowledge but it cannot keep a justified false belief distinct from an unjustified false belief, nor an unjustified true belief distinct from a justified false belief. Justification apart from truth and truth apart from justification are lost outside the JTB cell, which is the taxonomic expression of the familiar regress / circularity / dogmatism pressure.

reflection_text.4:
The JTB analysis is K = B ∧ T ∧ J with K → B. With only K and B as primitives the Truth × Justification 2×2 is coarse-grained to JT = K and B = ¬K = [J ∧ ¬T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ T ∧ B] ∨ [¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B]. K is a proper species of B and Belief is forced to do the work of three distinct profiles.

Round 4 consensus is stable and unanimous. The two problems are the same taxonomic loss described in two equivalent formulations.

* Justification is invisible once truth fails. J ∧ B ∧ ¬T is justified false belief, a properly supported warranted error, epistemically creditworthy though ¬T so not K on JTB. On a K/B only inventory it must be called mere Belief and is lumped with ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T unjustified false belief and with ¬J ∧ B ∧ T unjustified true belief. There is no state ‘justified non-knowledge’ in which to house warranted error. Justification ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when truth fails; it is only visible together with truth inside K. In grounding terms cashing J in K/B forces p justified by q, q by r… with no third epistemic status to stop the chain → infinite regress of beliefs-for-justification or K→J→K circularity/bootstrapping.

* Truth is invisible once justification fails. ¬J ∧ B ∧ T is unjustified true belief, true but lucky/accidental, epistemically defective so ¬J so not K on JTB. On a K/B only inventory it too must be called mere Belief and is lumped with J ∧ B ∧ ¬T and ¬J ∧ B ∧ ¬T. There is no state ‘true non-knowledge’ in which to house lucky truth. Truth ceases to be recognisable as an independent good when justification is absent; it is only visible together with justification inside K. In grounding terms this is the need for a stopping point: the regress can only be halted by a dogmatic foundational base of beliefs taken as justified simply by being held, or by circular bootstrapping K→J→K.

Hence Belief becomes the heterogeneous grab-bag J¬T ∨ ¬JT ∨ ¬J¬T. JTB can still mark JTB as Knowledge but cannot keep a justified false belief distinct from an unjustified false belief, nor an unjustified true belief distinct from a justified false belief. Justification and truth are no longer independently trackable outside the JT cell.

The two canonical cells JTB needs but a two-state ontology cannot accommodate are J¬T justified false belief and ¬JT unjustified true belief. The regress/circularity/dogmatism formulation is the dynamic grounding symptom of this static taxonomic loss. No material disagreement remains across colleagues; remaining nuance is verbal about phrasing the two problems as the two unmarkable non-knowledge cells versus regress vs arbitrary foundation/circularity, which are taken as mutually entailing. Gettier is explicitly excluded.
